Mughals adopted “Navroj” festival from – (a) Zoroastrians (b) Jews (c) Mongols (d) Turks U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2001 Ans. (a) Navroz festival was adopted from Persia (Iran). It was a national festival which was celebrated nineteen days. It had great signiﬁ cance during the Mughal period. The preparation of the festival used to begin quite long back. Abul Qadir Badauni stated Navroz as “Navroz-e-Jalali.” 27. (a) Manucci (b) Tavernier (c) William Finch (d) Abdul Hamid Lahori (e) None of the above/More than one of the above B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2018 Ans. (c) According to William Finch, five thousand to twenty thousand men worked for forty years to build the palace of forty pillars at Allahabad in Akbar's tenure. 28. During the Mughal period, the Madarsa which was specialized in the teaching of ‘Muslim Jurisprudence,’ was located in – (a) Lucknow (b) Delhi (c) Sialkot (d) Hyderabad (India) U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2016 Ans. (a) The teaching of ‘Muslim Jurisprudence’ was specialized in Lucknow Madrasa during Mughal period. Mulla Nizamuddin born in Sihali, 28 km from Lucknow was the originator of ‘Darse Nizami,’ the new curriculum which included Tafsir (exegesis of Quran), Hadith (tradition of Prophet Muhammad) and Fiqh (Islamic Jurisprudence). 29. Arrange the chronological order of the following options and ﬁ nd out the correct answer with the help of the given codes : 1. Ahilya Bai 2. Durgawati 3. Padmini 4. Tara Bai Code : (a) 1, 2, 3, 4 (b) 3, 2, 4, 1 (c) 3, 4, 1, 2 (d) 2, 1, 3, 4 U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2002 U.P. U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 2001 Ans. (b) Padmini was the queen of Chittor and the wife of King Rana Ratan Singh. In the battle, Khalji defeated Rana Ratan Singh at Chittor. After killing Rana Ratan Singh, Khalji wanted Rani Padmini to make his own by force. After that, Padmini decided to take ‘Jauhar’ which was similar to the Sati system. Rani Durgavati was a great Hindu warrior queen of Gondwana. After being defeated by Akbar in the war, she daggered and killed herself. Tara Bai Bhonsle was the queen of Chhatrapati Rajaram Bhonsle, She was acclaimed for her role in keeping alive the resistance against the Mughal occupation of Maratha territories after the death of her husband. Ahilya Bai was the Holkar Queen of the Maratha-ruled Malwa kingdom. Indore was occupied by the Holkar dynasty. Indian History General Studies B–311 30. Which one of the following is correctly matched ? (a) Khuldabad - Tomb of Shaikh Salim Chishti (b) Fatehpur Sikri - Tomb of Itmad-ud-Daula (c) Agra - Tomb of Aurangzeb (d) Delhi - Tomb of Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2010 Ans. (d) The famous Dargah or Tomb of Shaikh Salim Chishti is located in Fatehpur Sikri. Tomb of Itmad-ud-Daula is located in Agra and the tomb of Aurangzeb is situated at Khuldabad (Aurangabad). The tomb of Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan is situated in Delhi. Therefore, option (d) is correctly matched. 31. Arrange the following battles of the Mughal period in chronological order– 1. Battle of Ghaghra 2. Battle of Khanwa 3. Battle of Chausa 4. Battle of Samugarh Select the answer from the codes given below: (a) 2, 1, 3 and 4 (b) 1, 3, 2 and 4 (c) 3, 2, 1 and 4 (d) 2, 3, 1 and 4 Chhattisgarh P.C.S. (Pre) 2008 Ans. (a) The correct chronological order is- 1. The battle of Khanwa was fought between Rana Sanga and Babur in 1527. Babur consolidated the new Mughal empire in India by this victory. 2. The battle of Ghaghra was fought between Babur and Mahmud Lodi in 1529. Lodi was defeated by Babur. This was the last battle for Babur. 3. The battle of Chausa was faught between Mughal emperor Humayun and Sher Shah Suri in 1539. Humayun was defeated in this battle. 4. The battle of Samugarh was fought in 1658 between Aurangzeb and Murad Baksh with his elder brother Dara Shukoh in 1658. In this war, Dara Shukoh was badly defeated. 34. Arrange the following monuments in chronological order and select the correct answer from the codes given below : I. Rabia Daurani's Tomb, Aurangabad II. Sher Shah Suri's Tomb, Sasaram III. Humayun's Tomb, Delhi IV. Atala Mosque, Jaunpur Codes : (a) I, II, IV, III (b) IV, II, III, I (c) II, I, III, IV (d) III, IV, II, I U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2019 Ans. (b) Atala Mosque of Jaunpur was built by Ibrahim Shah Sharqi around 1408 AD. Sher Shah Suri (1540-45 AD) built his own tomb in Sasaram. The mosque-the Khayr-ul-manzil opposite to the Purana Qila in Delhi was constituted by whom? (a) Hamida Banu Begum (b) Salima Sultan (c) Jiji Anga (d) Maham Anaga U.P.P.C.S. (Pre 2018) Ans. (d) Maham Anaga constituted a madarsa named 'Khayr-ul- manzil' opposite to the Purana Qila in Delhi. Khayr-ul- manzil was a Madarsa established for the purpose of teaching but in the question, it has been termed as 'Mosque'. 38. (c) Jahangiri Mahal was built by Akbar in Agra. Rest of the options are correctly matched. 39. Which one of the following buildings is known as 'Shah- i-Fatehpur'? (a) Buland Darwazah (b) Turky Sultana ka Mahal (c) Jama Masjid (d) Shahjadi Umber ka Mahal Uttarakhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2016 Ans. (c) Fatehpur Sikri (City of Victory) was founded as the capital of Mughal Empire by Akbar in 1571. Various complexes of Mughal architecture at Fatehpur Sikri are Jama Masjid, Buland Darwaza, Punch Mahal, Tomb of Shaikh Salim Chisti etc. Jama Masjid of Fatehpur Sikri is also known as 'Shah-i- Fatehpur' or 'Shah-i-Sikri'. Fatehpur Sikri was listed among the world heritage sites by UNESCO in the year 1986. 40. With reference to the cultural history of India, consider the following statements: 1. White marble was used in making Buland Darwaza and Khankah at Fatehpur Sikri. 2. Red sandstone and marble were used in making Bara Imambara and Rumi Darwaza at Lucknow. Indian History General Studies B–313 Which of the following given above is/are correct? (a) 1 only (b) 2 only (c) both 1 and 2 (d) Neither 1 nor 2 I.A.S. (Pre) 2018 Ans. (d) Buland Darwaza is constructed using red sand stone along with white marble to decorate it. It was constructed by Akbar in 1602 A.D. to mark his victory over Gujarat. It is situated in Fatehpur Sikri in Agara. However white marble was not used in the construction of Salim Chisti's Khankah, instead it was used in making his tomb. Bada Imambada and Rumi darwaza both are situated in Lucknow and were built by Asaf-ud-daula. The central hall of Bada Imambada is 50 m. in length and 16 m in breadth. Its roof is more than 15m high and is without any pillar. This hall is world's biggest hall standing without using any wood, iron or stone beam. Its roof is built using just bricks and without beam or garter. Bricks and lime was used in its construction instead of stone or marble. Rumi darwaza which is main entrance gate was built using lime plaster and lime molding along with Lakhori bricks. Hence neither statement 1 nor statement 2 is correct. 41. During the Mughal period ‘Muallim ‘ was – (a) A tax (b) An administrative unit (c) A ruler (d) A ship U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2014 Ans. (*) Muallim or navigator was an employee on Indian merchant ships. He used to hold a spherical device on the ship to identify the position of stars and the sun. It helped him to identify the correct position of his ship. In the given options, option (d) seems to be near to the answer, but it is not an appropriate answer as Muallim was an employee/worker, not a ship. 42. Banjaras during the medieval period of Indian history were generally (a) Agriculturists (b) Warriors (c) Weavers (d) Traders I.A.S. (Pre) 2016 Ans. (d) Banjaras during the medieval period of Indian history were traders. They used to move from one place to another, sometimes with thousands of oxen, laden with food grain, salt, ghee and other daily stuﬀ . They were specialized in Caravan trading and also in textile embroidery, etc. 43. In the times of Mughals the region of Jharkhand was known as _______. (a) Aranya (b) Vananchal (c) Kukra (d) Atavi Jharkhand P.C.S. (Pre.) 2021 Ans (c) During the Mughal period, the Jharkhand area was known as Kukara.
